payload.selection_rationale: Single proposal (practice), taken as core almost verbatim. It matches how the file is already shaped: nine existing $CaseMutants entries (StopDisabled, StopCollapsed, etc.) already follow the ValidateSet-plus-hashtable-entry pattern this proposal extends, so adding a tenth is the smallest change that fits the grain of the code rather than inventing a new mechanism. It is grounded in measurement, not taste: the risk spike killed the exact Find/Replace pair 20/20 clean and 10/10 under load, and separately proved (via the StopDisabled stand-in, since EndingObeysSkip doesn't exist yet) that the shared Set-Mutation path already fails fast on a stale anchor rather than silently passing. The proposal's own over_engineering_flag is honoured rather than argued past: the popular answer here is to adopt Stryker.NET or PSMutant, and the proposal correctly rejects both as too large for one guard, needing a unit-test project the App deliberately doesn't have (window state is verified through --report/WindowCases, per the stack decision) or targeting the wrong language entirely. It touches nothing already known to be correct: MainWindow.xaml.cs's guard, WindowCases.ps1's L-002, and the SL-064 acceptance test are all left alone, matching the build-check's finding that the only gap is the missing ValidateSet value and hashtable entry. The one thing left genuinely open by the proposal itself -- whether the harness could ever misclassify a compile error or crash as a kill -- is carried forward honestly as a must-verify item rather than papered over, because the spike that would have settled it (mutant-killed-for-the-right-reason) ran out of turns before reaching a verdict.
payload.coherence_check: One proposal was handed to this synthesis; there is no second proposal's pieces to reconcile, and nothing here has yet been disagreed with by anybody. What I did check was internal consistency between three things the proposal itself draws on: the build-check's list of five missing criteria, the acceptance test's own check order, and the spike's measured evidence. They line up without a seam to redesign -- the proposed ValidateSet value, hashtable entry, Find/Replace pair and single Fail pattern map one-to-one onto the five 'missing' items build-check recorded, and the Find/Replace text is lifted verbatim from the exact patch the spike measured killing L-002 20/20 (not a re-derivation of it). The one place I did not paper over a gap: cross_domain_transfer's third invariant (mutant-killed-for-the-right-reason) is 'must-verify', not 'holds' -- that spike ran out of turns, so whether the harness could ever count a compile error or crash as a kill for this specific entry is unresolved by anything measured so far, and I've carried it forward as an open case rather than assuming it away. architecture_rules is empty by design: this slice adds one data-table entry to an existing PowerShell hashtable that a pre-existing shared function (Set-Mutation) already applies and validates the match-count of; there is no new import relationship or module boundary for a must_not_import rule to govern, and the one real invariant worth stating -- Find must match exactly once inside the real ShowFinalTopLevel body, not also inside sibling method RefreshTopLevel -- is a dynamic cardinality check the harness itself already enforces at run time with its own error message, not a fixed textual pattern I can safely regex against a file I have not read character-for-character without risking a rule that either matches nothing or fires on the nine other, correct, entries in the same table.

proposals.note: Taken essentially whole: the ValidateSet addition, the $CaseMutants entry with the spike's exact Find/Replace, the single topLevel.final Fail pattern, and the decision not to touch app code, WindowCases.ps1 or the acceptance test. Added on top: an explicit cases matrix separating the acceptance test's static text checks from the dynamic end-to-end run neither the acceptance test nor the build stage exercises, and an explicit empty architecture_rules with reasoning rather than leaving the field's absence unexplained.

components.name: EndingObeysSkip ValidateSet value
components.responsibility: Makes -Mutant EndingObeysSkip a legal argument by appending it after 'HookLocked' in the ValidateSet attribute. This is the exact check the repro test throws on today.
components.key_interactions: Read by PowerShell's own parameter binding before any mutation logic runs; also read as AST text by the SL-064 acceptance test.

components.name: $CaseMutants['EndingObeysSkip'] entry
components.responsibility: Wires the mutant to Case='L-002', File='src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs', with Find/Replace equal to the spike's measured patch (adds '&& !_skipNextRefresh' to the existing else-if) and one Fail pattern containing the literal 'topLevel.final'.
components.key_interactions: Consumed by the existing shared Set-Mutation (enforces exactly-one match, exits 1 on a stale anchor) and Test-CaseMutant (runs WindowCases.ps1 -Case L-002 against the mutated build and matches Fail patterns against its output). Its shape is copied from the StopDisabled/StopCollapsed entries, not invented.

components.name: 'All' roster (verify, patch only if needed)
components.responsibility: Ensures a full-suite run (-Mutant All) actually includes EndingObeysSkip. If All already enumerates $CaseMutants.Keys, nothing changes here; if it is a hard-coded list, the name is added to it.
components.key_interactions: This is the only path through which the mutant keeps 'standing' guard against regression on every routine full run, rather than only when named explicitly.

components.name: Mutation site (read-only anchor)
components.responsibility: ShowFinalTopLevel, the guard that must always show the scan's final TopLevel snapshot. Confirmed correct and untouched today; not edited by this slice, only targeted by the mutant's Find/Replace.

components.name: L-002 case (reused, unchanged)
components.responsibility: Asserts topLevel.final == true, reading == 0, and bytes/files match core at the scan's ending. Its assertion output is what the new Fail pattern must be able to match.

components.name: SL-064 acceptance test (reused, unchanged)
components.responsibility: The slice's own static, text-only check of the five criteria (ValidateSet value present, hashtable entry present and correctly wired, Find matches once inside the real method, Replace consults _skipNextRefresh, Fail mentions topLevel.final). Passing it is the slice's stated acceptance criterion; it is not modified to fit the entry.

contracts.name: WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant EndingObeysSkip
contracts.error_cases: Exits 1 if the Find anchor matches zero or more than one time in MainWindow.xaml.cs (Set-Mutation's stale-anchor guard). Exits 1 if L-002 passes against the mutated build (the mutant survived). Exits non-zero, and must not report 'killed', if the mutation causes a compile error or the app to crash before L-002 can even run its assertion.
contracts.notes: Exits 0 only when L-002 fails specifically on the topLevel.final line. Needs one app build plus one L-002 run, so needs the .NET 10 SDK (bootstrapped per Q-003 if no machine-wide 10.0 SDK is present).

contracts.name: WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant All
contracts.notes: Must now also apply and test EndingObeysSkip as part of the full mutant pass; this is what makes the guard 'standing' rather than only checkable on demand.

contracts.name: SL-064 acceptance test
contracts.error_cases: A throw in any of its checks exits 1.
contracts.notes: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tests/bugs/SL-064-EndingObeysSkipMutant.Tests.ps1 must exit 0. It is text/AST-only and needs no build, so the SDK gap on this machine does not block it.

key_decisions.decision: Use the risk spike's measured patch verbatim as Find/Replace: 'else if (!ReferenceEquals(final, _shownTopLevel))' becomes 'else if (!ReferenceEquals(final, _shownTopLevel) && !_skipNextRefresh)'. Do not also clear the flag or rewrite the method more broadly.
key_decisions.rationale: This is the only mutation with direct evidence behind it: 20/20 kills clean, 10/10 under load, 20/20 clean-build passes. Any other phrasing discards that evidence and has to be re-measured.

key_decisions.decision: Fail patterns: exactly one, containing the unescaped literal substring 'topLevel.final'. Do not add patterns for the reading or bytes symptoms.
key_decisions.rationale: topLevel.final False is the direct, deterministic consequence of the mutation. The spike saw the full three-symptom signature in only 19 of 20 runs, so keying on the secondary symptoms too would turn a real kill into an occasional false survivor. An unescaped dot matches both as a regex and as a substring/-like check, whichever the harness uses.

key_decisions.decision: Route the mutant through the existing shared Set-Mutation/Test-CaseMutant path with the entry shape copied from StopDisabled, rather than any bespoke logic.
key_decisions.rationale: The stale-mutation-site-goes-red spike's fail-fast-on-stale-anchor guarantee was proven only for mutants that go through Set-Mutation. Anything else would forfeit that guarantee for this entry specifically.

key_decisions.decision: Do not touch MainWindow.xaml.cs, WindowCases.ps1, or the SL-064 acceptance test.
key_decisions.rationale: build-check already confirmed the guard is correct as written and the acceptance test already specifies the target shape; this slice proves the guard, it does not change it, and editing the acceptance test to fit an entry would defeat the entry's purpose.

key_decisions.decision: Reject adopting a mutation-testing tool (Stryker.NET, PSMutant) for this slice.
key_decisions.rationale: Stryker.NET needs a unit-test project the App deliberately doesn't have (window state is verified via --report/WindowCases by project decision); PSMutant mutates PowerShell AST, not C#. Both would generate far more mutants than this one guard needs. The practice designer flagged this as the over-engineered path and that judgement is honoured rather than argued past.

key_decisions.decision: Name the mutant 'EndingObeysSkip', appended after 'HookLocked' in the ValidateSet.
key_decisions.rationale: Matches the name the acceptance test and slice record already use; ValidateSet order carries no meaning, so appending keeps the diff to the smallest possible addition.

cases.behaviour: invoke the mutant harness by name
cases.shape: -Mutant EndingObeysSkip is passed as the parameter value
cases.why: ValidateSet rejects an unlisted value before any mutation logic runs; this exact throw is the repro test's captured failure and the acceptance test's first check

cases.behaviour: look up which case and file a mutant targets
cases.why: an entry not wired to Case='L-002' and File='src/FsAnalyser.App/MainWindow.xaml.cs' would run against the wrong case or file, and the harness has no other way to know which one a mutant targets

cases.behaviour: apply the mutant's Find/Replace to the real source
cases.shape: the Find anchor's match count inside the current file is exactly one
cases.why: Set-Mutation exits 1 on zero or more than one match (proven generically by spike stale-mutation-site-goes-red); the anchor text must not also occur inside sibling method RefreshTopLevel or elsewhere, or the count guard fires for the wrong reason

cases.behaviour: the mutated guard decides whether to show the final snapshot
cases.shape: _skipNextRefresh is true when the scan ends
cases.why: this is the actual injected fault -- if Replace doesn't reference the flag, the mutant is inert and L-002 will pass against it, which is exactly what this slice must prevent from going unnoticed

cases.behaviour: the harness decides whether a mutant is killed
cases.shape: L-002's failure output contains the literal 'topLevel.final' failure line
cases.why: the acceptance test's Fail-pattern check requires this specific token; a pattern keyed on the reading/bytes symptoms instead would misclassify the 1-in-20 run (per spike) where only the final flag differed as a survivor

cases.behaviour: run the full mutant suite as normally scheduled
cases.shape: -Mutant All is invoked instead of naming EndingObeysSkip directly
cases.why: a mutant only stays 'standing' -- keeps biting on every routine run -- if All actually reaches it; if All is a fixed list rather than derived from $CaseMutants.Keys, the entry is reachable by name but silently absent from the regular full pass

cases.behaviour: kill the mutant end-to-end through the standing harness path
cases.shape: the mutated app is actually built and L-002 actually run against it, not hand-patched
cases.why: the acceptance test only parses WindowMutants.ps1 as text and needs no build, so nothing in this slice's own test proves the entry runs; the spike proved the hand-patch kills 20/20, but never through Set-Mutation/Test-CaseMutant itself

cases.behaviour: confirm the kill is attributable to the mutation, not a pre-existing failure
cases.shape: L-002 against the unmutated, clean build, applied and restored through the harness's own sandbox mechanism
cases.why: if L-002 already failed for an unrelated reason the harness would report a false kill; spike measured 20/20 clean passes by hand-patch, but validate must see the same from the harness's own restore path, not a scratch copy

cases.behaviour: distinguish a genuine kill from a broken mutation
cases.shape: the mutation causes a compile error or an app crash instead of a clean L-002 failure
cases.why: cross_domain_transfer's must-verify invariant (mutant-killed-for-the-right-reason) is exactly this: a compile error or crash must not be counted as 'killed'. Spike's hand-patch build succeeded and ran cleanly across 30 runs with no crash or compile error for this exact Find/Replace pair, and the killed-vs-not classification itself is shared, pre-existing Test-CaseMutant behaviour this slice does not modify -- judged not worth a dedicated test in this slice; the single required end-to-end run (the case above) will surface a misclassification immediately if one occurs

If -Mutant All is a hard-coded list rather than derived from $CaseMutants.Keys: the new name added to that list
whats_reused: Set-Mutation's exactly-once match check and its stale-anchor exit 1 (tests/window/WindowMutants.ps1)
_skipNextRefresh field already declared and used elsewhere in MainWindow.xaml.cs

cross_domain_transfer.source_domain: Clinical laboratory quality control (positive controls in assay runs)
cross_domain_transfer.pattern: Every assay run includes a positive control: a sample known to carry the target, and the run counts only if the control produces the SPECIFIC expected signal rather than any signal at all. Here the mutant is the positive control for L-002, the specific signal is the topLevel.final failure line, and a Find anchor that matches zero or multiple times is a control sample that doesn't actually contain the target.
cross_domain_transfer.rationale: Explains why the Fail pattern must be specific but not over-specific: keyed on a secondary, timing-dependent marker (reading/bytes, present in only 19/20 spike runs) it would falsely invalidate a real kill; keyed on any failure at all it would accept contamination such as a compile error being counted as a kill. That specificity rule is what decided the single-pattern, topLevel.final-only choice.

invariants.precondition: The control reacts reliably -- the mutant is killed deterministically.
invariants.evidence: Spike ending-obeys-skip-killed-every-run: 20/20 plus 10/10 under load with 8 of 16 cores busy; clean build passed 20/20.

invariants.precondition: The control actually contains the target -- the mutation applies exactly once, and a stale site goes red rather than silently running the clean build.
invariants.evidence: Spike stale-mutation-site-goes-red: with the StopDisabled stand-in on the shared Set-Mutation path, a stale anchor exits 1 and nothing is built. Holds for this entry only insofar as it uses Set-Mutation, which this design requires.

invariants.precondition: The run counts only on the specific signal -- a compile error, crash or missing report is never counted as a kill.
invariants.evidence: Spike mutant-killed-for-the-right-reason did not finish (ran out of turns before recording a verdict). Validate must run WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant EndingObeysSkip once for real, confirm exit 0 with the topLevel.final line actually matched, and check how the harness treats a build failure versus a kill.

prior_art.pattern: Mutants are applied to a throwaway sandbox copy so tracked source is never modified even if the run is killed mid-way -- the property WindowMutants' existing restore/sandbox mechanism must keep for this new entry.

Candidates are located by AST offset and applied as a pure splice; PSMutant is PowerShell-only, which is why it cannot replace a hand-authored C# anchor here. The anchored-text-match-exactly-once approach is the text-level stand-in for 'the fault is where you think it is'.

A per-mutant wall-clock timeout is the real safety net because a mutant can hang the run. Not needed here: across all 30 spike runs the mutated app exited, with L-002 reporting FAILED rather than hanging.
A subset re-run is a development convenience, not a measurement -- the same caution applies here: running -Mutant EndingObeysSkip alone at validate does not stand in for -Mutant All passing.

Mutation tools report compile errors and timeouts as their own statuses rather than as kills, because counting a mutant that fails to build as 'killed' inflates the score. The Fail-pattern specificity requirement is this harness's version of that separation.
prior_art.where: Stryker.NET mutant status model (Killed / Survived / CompileError / Timeout)

prior_art.pattern: A small number of targeted, hand-reviewed mutants on important code paths beats bulk generated mutants nobody acts on.
prior_art.where: Google, mutation testing in code review practice

channeled_experts: Stryker.NET maintainers: mutant status taxonomy, keeping CompileError/Timeout separate from Killed
PSMutant author: a mutation that never touches tracked source, and a recheck is not a measurement
Clinical lab QC practice: a positive control must give the specific signal, or the run is invalid
